findings.summary: The same failed attempt can enqueue two alerts when first observed in the flow bus and later in the run projection.
findings.evidence: Fresh Probe U: exit 0; failure of demo/REQ-001 T1/a1 is first represented by flow row flow-1, then by the run-state attempt with its ended_at one second later. Real build_events/page and NotificationOutbox store two different dedupe-key rows. bt_remote_events.py:143-152 suppresses flow duplicates only inside one current projection; from_flow identity at 176-178 differs from the attempt identity at 79, so sequential observations bypass durable dedupe. These fixtures demonstrate one semantic failure under both producer forms, not a measured frequency in a deployed run. R11 requires a stable key for the same event.

findings.summary: An unauthenticated Unicode OAuth state drops the callback connection instead of returning a controlled invalid-state response.
findings.evidence: Fresh Probe X: exit 0; real loopback gateway GET callback with synthetic code, query state=%C3%A9 and cookie flow_oauth_state="é" terminates its request with TypeError from hmac.compare_digest on non-ASCII strings. The handler error hook records TypeError and HTTP client gets RemoteDisconnected. server.py:198 does not validate ASCII before comparison. No state bypass, session issuance or whole-process denial of service is demonstrated; the existing one-use/replay protections remain.
